objective: Exercise real ZTF DR24 lightcurve retrieval and the existing native v0.2 feature engine on a deterministic bounded subset, independently of CPVS membership reconstruction.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Scientific Validation run 40296581372 on 2026-10-26 successfully acquired a 150-object DR24 Objects Table subset and ALeRCE evidence, but did not retrieve DR24 lightcurve epochs or invoke the feature engine on DR24 observations.
The existing feature engine requires normalized observations with mjd, fid, mag, and magerr and emits the frozen 42-feature v0.2 schema with input hash provenance.

baseline.description: Keep v0.2.0/v1.0.1 model, feature schema, class order, and scientific acceptance criteria unchanged. This smoke test does not alter training or inference artifacts.

expected_improvement: Retrieve real DR24 lightcurves for a deterministic bounded subset of the existing 150-object DR24 metadata sample.
Normalize documented DR24 HMJD, filter IDs, magnitude, magnitude uncertainty, and quality flags without fabricating measurements.
Run the existing native feature engine and retain per-object source hashes, normalized-observation hashes, feature eligibility counts, and failures.
Separate successful ingestion/feature execution from model inference and scientific validation claims.

reliability.before: DR24 evidence job checked Objects Table response schema and provenance only; no lightcurve-to-feature execution was verified.
reliability.after: Pending targeted DR24 lightcurve smoke workflow.

correctness.before: No verified real-DR24 feature-engine result in the scheduled workflow.
correctness.after: Pending real-data retrieval, 42-feature contract, hashes, and output report.
correctness.evidence: New script scripts/smoke_dr24_lightcurve_pipeline.py and report dr24_lightcurve_smoke_report.json.

evidence: The smoke test uses public DR24 lightcurves and the existing feature engine; it does not tune thresholds or modify model artifacts.
The live-data result and integration test status must be reviewed before this record can be finalized.

First real-data smoke run 40396734263 completed successfully for 12 objects; all 12 requests and native feature-engine calls succeeded, but every object had g_valid=162 and r_valid=0, yielding 19 finite features and 23 null/NaN features per object. Model inference remained NOT_RUN.

Artifact audit found the upstream 150-row DR24 object subset is the lexicographically first 150 OIDs and all rows map to one HATS sky partition; the first smoke selector then chose the highest ngoodobsrel objects. This is smoke evidence only and is not a representative survey sample.

The selector was revised to use stable SHA-256 ranking within the pinned eligible subset, with seed DR24-LIGHTCURVE-SMOKE-v1, and now records eligible-pool size and selection scope. Fresh CI and live-data rerun are required.

A second run after hash-ranking within the original 150-row subset still returned 12/12 g-only objects, confirming the limitation was upstream subset composition rather than only the per-object ranking.

The DR24 HATS index selector has now been changed to choose up to 15 evenly spaced index fragments and SHA-256-rank OIDs within each fragment. The pinned query contract records this method and seed; unit tests cover fragment spread and order-independent ranking. Fresh CI and live-source rerun are pending.

Latest Scientific Validation run 40398912969 exposed a contract mismatch: the manifest had moved to sha256_ranked_across_evenly_spaced_hats_index_fragments while the adapter still accepted only deterministic_lexicographic. The adapter now accepts the two explicit deterministic methods and validates seed/fragment_sample_count for fragment sampling; a regression assertion checks the new manifest contract. Re-run all checks on this head before considering the issue fixed.

Live source-backed workflow run 40399828150 failed in job 121842383690 with `SourceQueryError: oid is not deterministically sorted` after retrieving HATS data. The failure is an ordering/normalization contract mismatch, not evidence of an astronomical data-quality result.

Added `_normalize_and_sort_source_ids`: decode byte identifiers as UTF-8, strip whitespace, reject null/blank IDs, then stable-sort normalized strings before the fail-closed validator. Added a regression test for byte/string mixed IDs and null rejection; current-head tests and live rerun remain pending.
Latest source-backed run 40404485906 passed acquisition, the native feature-engine smoke step, and the external-evidence contract on head eb0852d395972c975d40111f75d01cdf75032826.

The verified smoke report has 12 candidate objects, 7 successful feature-engine executions, and 5 failures (`No g/r-band rows remained after filter normalization`). Zero of the 12 had 30+ valid points in both bands; model inference was NOT_RUN. This is PASS_SMOKE_ONLY evidence, not model or survey-wide scientific validation.
The report's selection pool contains 51 objects drawn from the pinned 150-row DR24 subset; it explicitly states this is not representative of the survey-wide population.

The workflow no longer auto-triggers the heavy job for every `work/dr24/**` branch. Heavy source acquisition remains available via explicit workflow_dispatch with run_heavy=true, schedule, main, or ci/heavy branches to avoid unnecessary repeated source downloads.
validation.blocker: The 5/12 no-g/r-row failures must be classified and reported; zero objects in this bounded sample meet 30-valid-points-per-band eligibility. This PR remains a smoke-test harness only. Do not run model inference or claim accuracy without a verified frozen artifact and eligible objects.

root_causes: The existing DR24 acquisition adapter retrieved object metadata only; it did not retrieve per-epoch lightcurve data or pass it to the feature engine.

findings: A successful metadata fetch is not evidence that the time-series ingestion and feature-generation path works on DR24.
Real-source integration checks must record source schema, raw-response hashes, normalized-observation hashes, eligibility counts, and explicit NOT_RUN states for downstream stages.

open_blockers: Fresh current-head format/lint/unit CI must pass after the workflow trigger change.
Document whether each of the five failures is expected source absence or an adapter/schema defect; retain the object IDs and raw response hashes.
Keep model inference NOT_RUN unless the frozen artifact is present and hash/schema are verified; no model accuracy or full scientific validation claim.
A larger, explicitly authorized DR24 sample is needed before any representative data-quality conclusion.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not use DR24 labels or metadata as independent ground truth unless a source-specific reference definition is documented.
Do not claim model accuracy, scientific validation, or CPVS resolution from a feature-engine smoke run.
Keep the immutable v0.2.0 baseline and v1.0.1 release artifacts unchanged.
Keep heavy source acquisition opt-in for work branches to avoid repeated downloads.
